Senses.Explanation: A conversational connective: 'being so' followed by 'then,' hence 'if so, then.' It occurs 5,426 times in 317 allowlisted texts. Chan encounter records give it a conspicuous turn-taking role: a questioner repeats or draws an inference from a respondent's answer, and that respondent may confirm, reverse, test, or reject the inference. Recorded replies call the inference wild talk, reverse its premise, block it with an image, ask for the student's own part, or demand how the claimed conclusion is carried out. These outcomes are deployments of the same connective, not new senses. Its distinctive role is the recurrent public-interview hinge where a proposed understanding becomes answerable to the next line.
Senses.Note: The high count reflects ordinary connective use across encounter dialogue. The phrase normally introduces the student's inference, but speaker role and the next response must be read from each exchange. Its demonstrative base, meaning 'being so,' and its following connective, meaning 'then,' remain one fixed compound here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云恁麼則學人無著身處也。師曰。是爾著身處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Nanquan-lineage exchange. An unnamed student is the exact speaker who infers, 'then I have nowhere to lodge my body'; the master immediately reverses the claim. The six-rung ladder does not name the student.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰恁麼則事同一家也。師曰。隔須彌在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄). The exact actor is an unnamed monk who says, 'if so, then the matter is the same as one household' (恁麼則事同一家也). No personal name remains after the six-rung review.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰恁麼則即相而無相也。師曰。也是狂言。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄). The exact actor is an unnamed monk who says, 'if so, then within form there is no form' (恁麼則即相而無相也). No personal name remains after the six-rung review.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云恁麼則音聲不入法界性也。師曰。離色求觀非正見。離聲求聽是邪聞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Nanquan-lineage exchange. An unnamed student is the exact speaker who infers, 'then sound does not enter the nature of the teaching-realm'; the respondent corrects him. The six-rung ladder does not name the student.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。恁麼則順正歸元去也。師曰。歸元何順。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Pozhao Duo section. The exact speaker is an unnamed monk from Niutou who infers, 'If so, then one returns to the source by following the correct'; Pozhao Duo challenges the claimed direction. All six rungs leave the monk personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：恁麼則絕於言句去也。師曰：夢裏惺惺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Tiantai Deshao section. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker who infers that the matter is cut off from words and phrases; Tiantai Deshao answers, 'awake inside a dream.' All six rungs leave the questioning monk personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧曰：恁麼則撒手那邊去也。師云：蝦跳不出斗。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄), in Xianglin Chengyuan's record. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker of 'if so, then I go over there with hands released' (恁麼則撒手那邊去也); Xianglin answers that a shrimp cannot jump out of a dipper. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passage do not name the monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「恁麼則均霑法利去也。」師云：「你本分事如何？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrong Xi (方融璽禪師語錄), memorial public exchange. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk: after Fangrong Xi answers that the timely eye is rain universally moistening all, the monk advances, 'then all equally receive the teaching's benefit.' The six-rung review found no personal name for this monk.
